tagline: A single dirt lane climbs from desert badlands to alpine country
intro: Bull Creek Pass is a 68-mile, single-lane dirt byway through Utah’s Henry Mountains, with rough sections, steep grades and blind curves. The Bureau of Land Management’s National Back Country Byway climbs nearly a mile from desert terrain toward alpine mountains, passing spruce and ponderosa slopes. BLM highlights canyons, cliffs and badlands, and allows six to eight hours for the drive. McMillan Springs Campground lies on the byway, with Lonesome Beaver Campground just north of it.

The route was built to provide access to the Henry Mountains for recreation and exploration. Mining had drawn people into Bromide Basin after prospectors found gold in 1889. Eagle City grew beside mills, but water entered deep mine shafts and a planned drainage tunnel went unfinished for lack of capital. By the start of World War I, the camp was almost abandoned.

Access roads lead into the mountains from Hanksville, Highway 95 and Highway 276. The ascent runs from desert badlands and buttes through canyons and cliffs, then wooded slopes, to Bull Creek Pass. The byway loops through the range between Capitol Reef and Canyonlands national parks.

moments.title: Eagle City
moments.text: Water helped end Eagle City’s gold rush. After prospectors found gold in Bromide Basin in 1889, owners of the Bromide and Oro mines built mills on Crescent Creek. The camp grew to as many as 100 people, with a store, hotel, doctor’s office and saloon. But shafts filled with water as they reached 300 feet deep. A drainage tunnel was planned and never completed for lack of money; in 1911 the Bromide Mill burned. Eagle City is now a ghost town. World War I drew away most of the remaining young men after the mill fire.

moments.title: Bull Creek Pass
moments.text: Bull Creek Pass marks the alpine part of a drive that starts on the desert floor. Below it, the road crosses badlands, buttes, canyons and cliffs before climbing through spruce and ponderosa. That variety extends to the animals inhabiting the Henry Mountains: mule deer, antelope, bighorn sheep, mountain lions and bison. The mountain loop gains nearly a mile in elevation.

moments.title: Mount Ellen
moments.text: In September 1895, Army signalmen used Mount Ellen as one end of a 183-mile visual message line. Mirrors eight inches across flashed signals toward Mount Uncompahgre in Colorado, with telescopes used to read them. Almon Harris Thompson had climbed the summit in June 1872 and named it for his wife, Ellen Powell Thompson. The mountain’s North Summit Ridge is the highest point in the Henry Mountains. Its height above the surrounding terrain exceeds 4,921 feet, the measure that makes it an ultra-prominent peak. Runoff belongs to the Fremont River watershed.

practical: Bull Creek Pass: Allow six to eight hours. Visit Utah advises a stout, high-clearance vehicle and checking with BLM in Hanksville before the drive. (checked 2026-10-11)
